title: Lightweight eval capture and lossy metrics PRD
author: Samir Patel
body:
Summary

This PRD describes a product-scoped initiative to capture lightweight evaluation signals and lossy aggregated metrics from production inference traffic. The goal is to enable rapid quality regression detection, SLO alignment, and low-cost longitudinal analysis without materially increasing latency, compute, or storage costs. The feature is targeted at hosted and dedicated customers who opt-in to telemetry capture and at internal Redwood teams that run continuous quality monitoring.

Problem statement

Teams building on Redwood lack a low-cost, low-latency mechanism to detect regressions in quality that are correlated with model changes, routing decisions, or customer configuration. Full-fidelity evals (storing entire request/response payloads) are expensive and create privacy/retention challenges. Existing per-token and latency metrics are necessary but insufficient to detect semantic regressions. There is a gap for a lightweight, lossy capture pipeline that provides high-signal indicators and can be run continuously across traffic slices.

Goals (what success looks like)

- Provide a production-safe ingest pipeline that samples and stores compact evaluation fingerprints for 0.5%-5% of requests (configurable per-tenant).
- Surface an automated regression alert when a selected set of evaluation metrics change by > X% relative to baseline (configurable).
- Keep end-to-end p99 added latency < 1ms and added per-request cost < 0.2% for sampled requests.
- Ensure retention and privacy controls: rolling window default 30 days, opt-out per-tenant, and PII redaction rules enforced before storage.
- Provide integration points for Redwood Optimize and Console dashboards to visualize trends and link to example traces and prompt-sets.

Non-goals

- This PRD does not attempt to replace the Eval Harness or manual human evaluations. It is a lightweight signal layer for continuous monitoring.
- It is not intended to store verbatim user data or full context windows for long-term retention.

User personas

- Platform engineer (internal): wants automated alerts aligned to SLOs and short diagnostic traces to speed triage.
- Product engineer (customer): wants to know if a model variant rollout caused quality regressions for a given route.
- SRE/Oncall: wants low-noise signals to inform incident response and rollback decisions.

High-level approach

1. Sampling policy: per-tenant sampling rate (0.5% default), with route-level overrides and burst sampling for canary rollouts.
2. On-request transform: compute and persist compact fingerprints (hashes, normalized token counts, top-k logits summary, embedding sketch) and lightweight judgement heuristics (e.g., syntactic validity, token-length drift, repetition score).
3. Aggregation and lossy storage: aggregate at 1m and 1h windows, store quantized histograms and differential summaries rather than raw text.
4. Alerting and visualization: allow customers and internal teams to declare metric baselines and thresholds; wire alerts into Console and Slack.

Key metrics (success criteria)

- Detection precision: >75% of true regressions detected within 24 hours on testbed runs with seeded regressions.
- Alert false-positive rate: <5% per 30-day rolling window.
- Added p99 latency: <1ms on sampled requests (measured in staging).
- Storage delta: <100GB/month per 100k RPS of sampled traffic (default sampling).

Requirements (functional and non-functional)

| ID  | Requirement description                                                                      | Priority |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
| F-01| Sampling: enable per-tenant and per-route sampling rates, with canary override API.           | Must     |
| F-02| Compute a compact evaluation record per sampled request: {request_hash, response_hash, short_stats, embedding_sketch}. | Must     |
| F-03| Redaction: PII detection and redaction pipeline runs before any storage.                     | Must     |
| F-04| Storage: store aggregated histograms and time-series; raw text is discarded within ingest.   | Must     |
| F-05| Baselines: allow users to register a baseline window and compare new metric windows to the baseline. | Should   |
| F-06| Alerts: configurable alert rules with automatic suppression during controlled rollouts.      | Should   |
| F-07| Dashboards: prebuilt Console dashboards showing signal trends, cold-start flags, and cohort comparisons. | Should   |
| N-01| Latency: added p99 latency for sampled requests <1ms.                                        | Must     |
| N-02| Cost: monthly cost impact per tenant must be forecastable via the Console.                   | Must     |
| N-03| Privacy: support per-tenant opt-out, retention config (7/30/90 days), and export deletion.   | Must     |

Data model (compact records)

We store only compact, typed strings and small arrays. Example record fields:

- request_hash: sha256 hex (string)
- response_hash: sha256 hex (string)
- top_token_ids: top-3 token ids (comma-separated string)
- repetition_score: numeric bucket label (e.g. low|medium|high)
- embedding_sketch: base64 of 128-bit locality-sensitive sketch
- length_bucket: short label (s|m|l|xl)
- route_id, tenant_id, model_variant_id (strings)
- sampled_at_iso (string)

Retention and compliance

- Default retention: 30 days. Tenant can choose 7/90.
- PII redaction: run regex and ML-based PII detectors; if detection confidence > 0.8, drop textual context and mark record with pii_flag=true.
- Data deletion: support immediate tenant-triggered purge by request_hash range and tenant_id.

Privacy note: this system is opt-in for customers by default and will not be enabled for customers in restricted regions until legal review.

Rollout plan

1. Prototype (Q1 2026): ingest pipeline and sketch compute in staging; run against internal traffic and synthetic regressions.
2. Pilot (Q2 2026): onboard 3-5 trusted customers; provide Console beta dashboards and alerting.
3. GA (Q3 2026): enable self-serve in Console with default sampling and billing SKU.

Rollout steps (detailed)

1. Implement lightweight SDK hooks in serving runtime to compute sketches and short_stats.
2. Add PII redaction stage in the ingest path with a safe-mode to drop text.
3. Build aggregation worker that produces quantized histograms and differential deltas.
4. Create Console surfaces: baseline setup UI, trend graphs, alert editor, and per-tenant cost estimator.
5. Legal & security review, add data processing agreement language for opt-in customers.

Open questions

- Which sketch algorithm balances recall vs storage for semantic similarity? (SimHash vs MinHash vs learned sketches)
- How should we encode model-version drift when customers pin custom models?
- Billing model: per-sample charge vs sampling-tier subscription — preference from revenue is sampling-tier subscription.

Risks and mitigations

- Privacy/regulatory risk: mitigate via opt-in default, strong redaction, regional gating.
- Noise/alert fatigue: add adaptive thresholding and suppression windows; provide manual tuning.
- Runtime regressions: isolate compute into async path where possible; fallback to no-op sampling if CPU pressure detected.

Ownership and stakeholders

- Product owner: Samir Patel (Product)
- Engineering lead: Arielle Chen (Serving Runtime)
- SRE/Telemetry: Owen Park (Eng Platform)
- Legal/Privacy: Leah Gomez (Security & Compliance)

Appendix A — Example sampled record (format)

request_hash, response_hash, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant_id, top_token_ids, repetition_score, embedding_sketch, length_bucket, sampled_at_iso
abc123...,def456...,tenant-123,route-search,variant-r1,345,78,low,qGZ...base64...,m,2026-01-12T14:22:03Z

Appendix B — Console mockups and alerting flows

- Baseline config UI: dropdown for baseline window and auto-calc button.
- Trend view: stacked area of metric deltas, heatmap of cohorts, link to sample traces.
- Alert editor: metric selector, percent-change threshold, suppression window, and rollout auto-suppression checkbox.
